entries.body:
Summary of work so far (stage 1 of 3 read; stages 2 and 3 not yet released):

Stage 1 facts (paths relative to /task/fixtures):
- stage-1/UPDATE.md:1-3. Window 08:00-09:30 UTC. ingress-a began returning 5xx for payments-api shortly after a deploy.
- stage-1/deploy/deploys.log:1. 2031-03-06T08:14:28Z, payments-api build 6.25.3-646f (previous 6.24.1) rolled out 100% by deploy-bot. Lines 2-7 are deploys of other services (billing-svc, quotes-api, inventory-svc, orders-api, shipping-api) between 08:48 and 09:26; they look irrelevant.
- stage-1/config/payments-api.yaml (repo defaults, overridden by release notes and APPLIED records):
  - line 7: clients.tax-engine.timeout_ms 2500
  - line 11: database.pool.max_size 48
  - line 12: acquire_timeout_ms 5000
  - line 14: cache ttl_s 120
- stage-1/deploy/release-notes-6.25.3-646f.md:
  - line 5: clients.tax-engine.timeout_ms lowered from 2500 to 800 ("fail fast").
  - line 17: db.pool.max_size lowered from 48 to 10 "to fit the shared-db connection quota".
  - line 14: ff-legacy-export removed (was 0%).
  - Current effective values as of stage 1: timeout_ms=800, pool max_size=10 (both release-note defaults; no APPLIED records seen yet).
- stage-1/ops/oncall-notes.md:5-6 (informal). 08:29 many tax-engine timeouts. 08:39 on-call suspects the timeout default change and is asking for a mitigation.
- stage-1/logs/ingress-a.log:80. First 5xx at 08:16:11, status=503, rt=4.623s, upstream_error="upstream timeout".
- stage-1/logs/payments-api.log:
  - Tax-engine errors: "upstream call tax-engine timed out after 800ms (attempt 1/1)", repeated from line 153 (08:15:33) through at least line 443 (08:44); dozens of occurrences.
  - DB pool: "db pool wait ...ms (in_use 10/10)" only 7 times (e.g. line 175 at 08:17:35 waited 2234ms; line 204 waited 1442ms).
  - Background noise: gc pauses, dns refresh retry succeeded, disk usage, TLS cert expires in N days.

Leading hypothesis: CLIENT_TIMEOUT_TOO_LOW. The tax-engine timeout of 800ms (release notes line 5) is below normal tax-engine latency. Remedy would be RAISE_CLIENT_TIMEOUT.
- Alternative still possible: DB_POOL_EXHAUSTED (pool max_size 10, release notes line 17). It is less frequent so far and must be watched in later stages.
- Not yet checked: actual tax-engine normal latency, and the timeline/frequency of the tax-engine timeouts after line 443.

Next steps:
- Reply {"action":"advance"} to release stage 2 and read all new files, especially any change log with APPLIED/PROPOSED records that change timeout_ms or pool max_size. Later APPLIED records win.
- Re-check whether symptoms shift (e.g. timeouts stop and pool exhaustion grows).
- Then advance to stage 3 and repeat.
- Final answer needs: the current effective value at the end of stage 3, plus evidence refs for (1) the current symptom, (2) the record setting the current value, and (3) the originating change (likely release-notes line 5 or 17).

Stage 2 of 3 released.
# Stage 2 of 3 (09:30-10:30 UTC)

On-call applied a mitigation (see stage-2/deploy/changes.log). The tax-engine timeouts stopped,
but ingress-a still returns 503s for payments-api with a different error. New files below.
